note: Every incoming transfer with at least 25 credited events, ranked by what he did last season. PRODUCTION is opponent-adjusted -- the level of schedule he faced is subtracted before anything is compared -- and is expressed on the recruiting composite's own 0.70-1.00 axis so the two columns sit side by side. The star equivalents are fitted from this year's roster (the mean composite at each star level, split at the midpoints), not asserted. RATED IS NOT ONE THING, AND THE GAP MEANS SOMETHING DIFFERENT IN EACH CASE -- use the SOURCE column and the filter beside it. • High-school composite: the number is what recruiting services said before he played, so a positive gap is the case this whole page exists to show -- recruiting did not see him. • Portal valuation: the number was assigned when he entered the portal, AFTER the season shown here, and rescaled onto the recruiting axis. It is a second opinion about the same play, so the gap measures agreement between two judgements rather than a miss; it is the weakest reading on the page and is the majority of rows. • Never rated: nobody assigned a number at all, and the blank is shown as a blank rather than as the 0.70 replacement floor, because a floor is an absence and subtracting from it would manufacture a large gap out of missing data. THE RATINGS ON THIS PAGE ARE READ BY NOTHING. The event counts behind them are not inert: since 2026 they feed net returning production, summed per team, with incoming quarterbacks counted once because a team plays one. So a team's rating can move when it signs a producer -- on how much he played, never on the number shown here.
